ops.title: Why the yasyf-home Tailscale exit node fell back to DERP (slow) and the real fix — an AT&T BGW320-505 Fixed DHCP Allocation was shadowing IP Passthrough to the eero; plus how to drive the BGW admin UI from the host.
ops.body:
The exit node **yasyf-home** (100.88.252.58) is the macOS fleet host, which sits behind an **eero** mesh (router mode, LAN 192.168.4.0/22, host at 192.168.4.24) behind an **AT&T BGW320-505** fiber gateway (192.168.1.254, public WAN 104.1.90.148). Symptom (2026-07): the laptop's exit traffic rode a cross-Pacific DERP relay (~20× throughput collapse; measured direct 55 MB/s vs DERP 2.8 MB/s) because a **double NAT** killed the inbound UDP path.

**Root cause (took two wrong hypotheses to find):** IP Passthrough was ALREADY correctly configured on the BGW (ippass.ha: allocmode=passthrough, passmode=dhcps-fixed, MAC=eero 24:2d:6c:9a:4e:83) and had been for 6+ months. The blocker was a separate **Fixed DHCP Allocation** on ipalloc.ha binding the eero MAC → private 192.168.1.64. That reservation SHADOWS passthrough: every eero DHCP DISCOVER matched the reservation and got the private lease before passthrough could hand out the public IP. So 6 months of eero reboots never worked, and — critically — **a BGW reboot would NOT have fixed it** (the reservation is persistent config).

**The fix:** on ipalloc.ha, convert the eero from "Fixed Allocation" back to "Address from DHCP pool" (removes the reservation), then reboot the eero (eero app) so it re-DISCOVERs → passthrough hands it the public 104.1.90.148 → double NAT collapses → direct WireGuard path. Verified: laptop→yasyf-home `via 104.1.90.148:41641` (was DERP sfo); status laptop CurAddr now non-empty. Note BGW passthrough is NOT a pure bridge — traceroute hop2 stays 192.168.1.254 (BGW still forwards) but the 2nd NAT is gone, which is all that matters.

**Driving the BGW admin from the host** (all read/POST over plain http to 192.168.1.254, no cookiesync): login = GET /cgi-bin/login.ha with a cookie jar (first GET only sets the session cookie + shows "Access Code Required"; the SECOND GET renders the real form with a 64-hex `nonce`), then POST `nonce` + `password`=N literal `*` chars + `hashpassword`=lowercase md5(deviceAccessCode+nonce) + `Continue=Continue`; success = `302 → /cgi-bin/home.ha` (a bad code re-renders the login form). **Repeated FAILED logins lock out** → one attempt per phase, stop on failure. The Device Access Code is on the unit's label; the user keeps it in their password manager (never persisted here — used from a mode-600 file via stdin/--data-urlencode, then shredded). ipalloc.ha edit = two-step POST: `ConnHost_1_1=Allocate` (302, selects the row) → GET → `alloc_1_1=normal|<privateIP>` + `Save=Save`. BGW restart = POST /cgi-bin/restart.ha `Restart=Restart`. Full incident + form map: cc-notes note a7299659, log db56b30c. Remote-safety pattern used: a detached local watchdog (PID reparented to launchd) probing internet every 20s, auto-restoring a private reservation then BGW-restart on sustained outage — needed 0 reverts. Still open: host en0 wired-Ethernet restore (still `status: inactive`). See [[host-serving-migration-2026-07]], [[hermes-model-plane-egress]].
